request.spec:
Each user has a locale (a select on the screen, en unless chosen, saved per user, no audit line).
Under de, every figure the screen shows that user (amounts, due figures, totals, rates, shares,
cuts: any cell whose whole text is a number with two decimals) is shown as 1.234,56 (a dot every
three digits, a comma before the decimals); under en as before. Entries are typed with a dot as
before, and exports and audit lines are unchanged.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user has a locale (a select on the screen, en unless chosen, saved per user, no audit line).
Under de, every figure the screen shows that user (amounts, due figures, totals, rates, shares,
cuts: any cell whose whole text is a number with two decimals) is shown as 1.234,56 (a dot every
three digits, a comma before the decimals); under en as before. Entries are typed with a dot as
before, and exports and audit lines are unchanged.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Users can now choose a locale, and under `de` every figure on the screen shows as `1.234,56`. With `bin/e2e`, the main locale test and scenario 1 pass, but **scenarios 2 and 3 still fail**. Each fails on one line that looks wrong in the spec itself, not on anything locale-related.

**The two remaining failures:**
- **Scenario 3, line 1124 (and again at line 1204):** it expects the parent sheet to read the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. The same test sets the parent to `` `${sheet}-p` `` (line 1036) and its audit check expects `value=${sheet}-p`, so this looks like a placeholder that was never filled in. No app could pass that line.
- **Scenario 2, line 678:** it expects a viewer pressing "generate plans" to get a count of 0. The app has always refused every change by a viewer with an error, and generating plans has no exception for viewers. Allowing it would change a permission rule the locale request doesn't mention, so I left it alone. Tell me if you want it changed.

To check that nothing later in those two scenarios breaks, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with just those two lines adjusted. Both scenarios then passed all the way through, and I deleted the copy. The real spec is untouched.

**What I changed:**
- **Saving the locale:** a new `user_locale` table (`V88`) and `GET`/`PUT /api/users/{user}/locale` routes under `locale/`. The locale is saved per user name, the same on every sheet. It is `en` until chosen, only `en` and `de` are accepted, and it writes no audit line.
- **The control:** a locale select with a save button and the current value, shown next to the signed-in user (`features/locale/UserLocale.tsx`).
- **Showing figures:** `features/locale/LocaleFigures.tsx` wraps the screen. Under `de` it rewrites any element whose whole text is a number with two decimals. Switching back to `en` restores the original text.
  - **Upside:** it covers every figure without touching each feature.
  - **Downside:** it rewrites the page text after React draws it, so it doesn't follow the app's usual patterns. Labels inside dropdown options are left alone, and typed entries, exports and audit lines are unchanged.
- **Rate limit raised:** the test sets a rate of `12345.67`, but rates were capped at 999.99 (the database column, the server rule and the form check). I raised the cap to 99999.99 in all three, including a migration (`V89`) that widens the column.

**Port clash:** `bin/e2e` uses `PORT=3002` from your shell, and something else was already running on that port, so I ran the tests with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`.
